title: Decision Unit Memorandum: Unemployment Insurance Appeals Decisions and Their Effects
content:
The decision on an appeal under Unemployment Insurance Appeals affirms, reverses or modifies the appealed determination, or, on the Board of Review only, remands it for a new hearing; it applies the docket's burden and standard of proof, and when only the other party is absent the decision rests on the evidence presented. Decisions are targeted within the docket's decision target days after filing. Where the docket pays when due, benefits are paid for weeks the decision finds payable as soon as it is issued, even if the other party appeals further, provided the claimant certified those weeks; if a later decision reverses it, the benefits paid become an appeal-reversal overpayment. A decision reversing an overpayment determination cancels the overpayment and one affirming it resumes recovery; a decision reversing a denial of charge relief relieves the employer's charges; a decision reversing or modifying a contribution rate causes a corrected rate notice, with contributions already paid above the corrected rate credited to the employer's account.

## 1. Outcomes available

| Outcome | Lower-authority dockets | Board of Review |
|---|---|---|
| affirm | yes | yes |
| reverse | yes | yes |
| modify | yes | yes |
| remand for a new hearing | no | yes |

The decision is issued and mailed; the appeal then stands at decided status.

## 2. Proof and absence

The decision applies the burden and standard of proof fixed for the docket. Where only the other party — not the appellant — is absent, the decision rests on the evidence presented.

## 3. Paying when due

On a docket that pays when due, benefits are paid as soon as the decision is issued for each week that (1) the decision finds payable and (2) the claimant certified. Payment is made even if the other party appeals further.

A week the claimant did not certify is not paid under this clause. If a later decision reverses the favorable one, the benefits paid become an appeal-reversal overpayment (a Benefit Overpayment Accounts matter).

## 4. Effects on the appealed record

| Kind of record appealed | Outcome | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| overpayment determination | reversed | the overpayment is cancelled |
| overpayment determination | affirmed | recovery of the overpayment resumes |
| denial of charge relief | reversed | the employer's charges are relieved (Employer Benefit Charging) |
| contribution rate | reversed or modified | a corrected rate notice issues, and contributions already paid above the corrected rate are credited to the employer's account (Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts) |

*Restated for the employer:* where a reversed or modified rate leaves contributions already paid at the appealed rate higher than the corrected rate calls for, the part paid above the corrected rate is credited to the employer's account.
